result:
Solution 1 is the most likely to be correct, with answer 6.

Solutions 2 and 3 rest on claims that don't hold up. Solution 2 asserts that every class reduces to trivalent graphs via IHX, but that reduction applies to graph-complex or Lie-type settings, not to a uniform valency bound on cohomology classes of $M_{g,m}$. Its sharpness argument is also invalid, since a graph with all vertices of degree at most 2 is not excluded by the Euler constraint alone. Solution 3 confuses the cohomology ring with quiver representations, its example relation $xy - z^2$ is not a valid description of $H^*(M_{0,3})$, which is a point, and its degree-counting argument has no real support.

Solution 1 cites a specific framework: ribbon quivers from the Kontsevich–Takeda–Vlassopoulos work on pre-Calabi–Yau structures and TQFT. Its valency-6 bound matches my recollection of that line of work, though I can't verify the exact statement from memory. Its averaging argument is heuristic, and the sharpness step is only sketched, so I'm not fully certain of the value. Still, it is the only candidate grounded in a plausible known framework.

CHOICE: 1
